result.reason: Both items directly concern Rabbi Yoḥanan's ruling about consecrating stolen property when ye'ush has not yet occurred, which fits squarely under the 'Kinyanim & Ye'ush' heading that discusses ye'ush and its role in establishing ownership of stolen objects.
Both items explain the symbolic logic behind the markers (orlah→potsherds yield no benefit; graves→lime is white like bones), which is precisely what the 'Symbols Explained' prose section describes.

Both items together constitute Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's qualification that marking is only required during shmitta (item 1) and the reason why marking is unnecessary during other years — the haliteihu principle (item 2) — which is precisely what the 'RSBG Position' prose describes.

The passage describes exactly what the tzenuim would do — set aside coins and declare the kerem revai desacralized onto them — which matches precisely the prose of 'Chasidim Extra' (candidate 1), not the challenge to Rabbi Yochanan in candidate 2.

Both items form a continuous argument challenging Rabbi Yochanan — item 1 raises the possibility that the tzenuim passage is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's individual opinion (not a stam mishna), and item 2 immediately refutes that escape route by citing Rabbi Yochanan's own rule that halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel — exactly the challenge described in heading 0's prose.

All four items deal with the breira resolution — the reinterpretation of the tzenuim's declaration from past to future tense, the challenge from Rabbi Yochanan's equation of tzenuim with Rabbi Dosa, and the baraita showing Rabbi Dosa's evening declaration — which is precisely what the 'Breira Solution' prose discusses, including the parallel to Rabbi Dosa's le'itotei erev ruling.

All seven items deal with the gemara's debate over reversing the baraita (Rabbi Yehuda vs Rabbi Dosa), the proof that Rabbi Yehuda does not hold breira from the wine-purchasing mishna, and the resulting contradiction in Rabbi Yochanan's own positions regarding breira — exactly the content described in the 'RY No Breira' prose section.

All five items form a continuous chain — retraction, the second-thief mishna, the derived principle (zeh lefi she'eino shelo), the question of why follow that stam, and the supporting verse — which is precisely the content described in candidate 0's prose about Rabbi Yochanan finding the other stam mishna and deriving the reshut principle.

Both items present Abaye's elaboration on why the tzenuim and Rabbi Dosa would not necessarily accept each other's rulings — exactly the content described in the 'Abaye View' prose about motivational differences between the ganav and aniyim cases.

All three items form Rava's single argument: he introduces his alternative claim (item 1) that the tzenuim's ruling follows Rabbi Meir, then explains why Rabbi Meir's view (ma'aser is mammon gavoha yet the Torah treats the owner as owner for redemption, items 2-3) makes the tzenuim case non-contradictory — exactly what the 'Rava View' prose describes.

All three items together constitute exactly the gezeira shava between kerem revai and ma'aser sheni via the word 'kodesh,' and the derivation that the owner has standing to desacralize even fruit not fully his — precisely the content described in the 'KR-Ma'aser Link' prose.

The passage directly states the principle that mafkir requires the object to be in one's possession ('ki itei birshuto hu d'matzei mafkir lei'), which is the exact Aramaic quoted and analyzed in the 'Redemption vs. Mafkir' prose section.

The passage describes exactly what the 'ID as Dosa' prose discusses: Ravina's suggestion that he would have identified the tzenuim as Rabbi Dosa himself to avoid a difficulty for Rabbi Yochanan, which matches the current placement precisely.
